hypotheses.subject: io-shop autoscaler / replica capacity
hypotheses.summary: Traffic to io-shop rose (request_volume climbing from ~1200/min to a plateau of 5400/min starting ~21:46) and the autoscaler kept adding and then immediately reclaiming capacity: cpu_limit_cores flaps between 3.0 and 6.0 every 1-3 minutes straight through the incident, even after request_volume flattens out at 5400 from 21:56 onward. Each time capacity drops back to 3 cores while cpu_used_cores is pegged at or above 3, latency spikes into the hundreds/thousands of ms, then partially recovers when the limit jumps back to 6. This is the signature of a scaling controller that will not settle rather than of capacity simply being outgrown - a plateaued, sized-once capacity would hold one value, not oscillate after demand stopped climbing.

An alternative reading of the same climb: request_volume grew roughly 4.5x (1200 to 5400/min) in about 10 minutes, well beyond what the service's steady 3-core baseline was provisioned for, and the resulting queuing produced the latency spikes seen from 21:52 onward. This is weaker than the autoscaling explanation because cpu_limit_cores is not held at a single value throughout - it visibly toggles between 3.0 and 6.0 - which is the specific signal that points to a controller not settling rather than plain undersizing.

No deploys or config/flag changes were recorded anywhere in the two hours before or during the incident, and the rollout is fully converged on a single revision, so code, configuration, and in-flight rollout splits are all ruled out. The account-page ClientDisconnected errors in the logs are a symptom of shoppers timing out on the slow responses, not a distinct root cause; no dependency-specific failures appear in the logs.

supporting_evidence.claim: Deployment of io-shop has converged: all 3 replicas are running the same revision.
account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection
